subject: Chat graceful degradation & client retry guidance for high-latency token bursts
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Perrin <lauren.perrin@fastretail.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Chat graceful degradation & client retry guidance for high-latency token bursts

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the call earlier. We confirmed a region-wide episode this morning that increased tail latency for streaming chat endpoints for a subset of sessions. I wanted to send a concise set of immediate mitigations you can apply client-side plus what we're doing server-side.

What happened (short): some shards experienced reordering of token assembly under heavy KV-cache warmup coupled with a kernel scheduling delay, which caused delayed final tokens for long-lived streaming sessions.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations (apply in this order):
1) Client backoff/partial-resume: if you detect a >1s gap between streamed chunks, retry the request with the same conversation id and with resume=true. See snippet attached (client-retry-snippet.patch).
2) Reduce chunk target size: set max_stream_chunk_tokens to 16 for sensitive UI flows where perceived latency matters.
3) Enable prefix KV caching sooner: send a short background request after user start-typing to warm prefix cache (we include recommended timings below).
4) Fallback route: use the low-latency stable variant (model: redwood-llama-lean-v1) for sessions flagged as interactive; this sacrifices a small amount of throughput for lower p95 latency.

Server-side actions we're taking:
- Rolling kernel scheduling fix to affected edge shards (in progress).
- Increased aggressive KV-cache pre-warm thresholds for chat sessions.
- Adding a mitigation router that will automatically route affected sessions to healthy replicas if token assembly latency spikes.

Attachments: latency-diagnosis-20261105.pdf (short diagnostic), client-retry-snippet.patch (code).

We'll post updates to this thread as the rollouts complete. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min working session to help wire the retry patterns into your clients.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Chat graceful degradation & client retry guidance for high-latency token bursts

Hi Lauren — quick answers and an actionable plan: 

1) Duplicate tokens: if you use resume=true we attach an idempotency token to the resumed request so the server deduplicates overlapping tokens. Properly implemented, clients should not see duplicates. The attached patch includes a small client-side marker to suppress duplicates until the server confirms resume.

2) ETA for server-side router fix: we have a staged rollout targeting full coverage in ~6 hours. If the rollout fails or you prefer immediate isolation, enable the fallback model (redwood-llama-lean-v1) for interactive sessions — that is immediate and reversible in your control plane.

Practical config changes we recommend you push today (examples):
- client.conf: 
  max_stream_chunk_tokens: 16
  resume_on_gap_ms: 800
  resume_idempotency: true
  early_kv_warm: true

- Example backoff loop (pseudocode):
  attempt = 0
  while attempt < 3:
    resp = stream_request(conversation_id, resume=(attempt > 0))
    if resp.last_chunk_time_gap < 800ms: break
    sleep(200 * (attempt+1))
    attempt += 1

We will also create a temporary per-account routing policy for FastRetail so your sessions are prioritized on healthy replicas while we finish the kernel patch. Sergio will coordinate the policy change with you.

If you give us a 30-min slot this afternoon we'll help with a quick patch rollout on your client and activate the per-account policy.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Perrin <lauren.perrin@fastretail.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident note: token assembly latency spike on 2026-11-05 — summary & next steps

Hi Lauren —

Short postmortem summary and follow-up actions per our promise on the call. Thanks again for partnering closely while we investigated.

What we observed: between 09:03–09:47 PST on 2026-11-05 a small cohort of edge replicas experienced non-deterministic token assembly delays triggered when KV-cache misses coincided with a kernel preemption event. The symptom was prolonged gaps between streamed chunks; p95 increased from ~120ms to ~980ms for affected sessions.

Impact: ~1.6% of streaming chat sessions in the us-west region were affected. FastRetail saw visible customer chat slowdowns for a subset of end users during your soft launch window; we recognize the impact to user experience.

Root cause: an internal kernel scheduling regression plus a thresholding bug in the KV-cache warmup heuristics.

Actions completed:
- Kernel scheduling fix deployed to all affected shards (rolled out 2026-11-05 13:20 PST).
- KV-cache warmup threshold corrected and increased prewarm cadence.
- Temporary per-account routing policy enabled for FastRetail during the evening of 2026-11-05.

Planned actions:
- We will ship an additional safety check to the streaming router to detect token-assembly gaps and auto-failover to healthy replicas (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Add a configurable per-account knob in the console to toggle low-latency fallback models (ETA: 1 week).

Compensation: we will issue a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of streaming request charges for the affected usage window — Sergio will follow up with the billing confirmation.

Attachments included: latency-diagnosis-20261105.pdf (diagnostic graphs, shard logs)

If you'd like a technical walk-through of the PDF, we can schedule a 45-min postmortem session next week; response options are Mon/Tue morning PST.

Best,

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
